name: workflow_interview
title: A module ask is interviewed, then drafted as "Your workflow" in the person's words

steps.remove_module: Car Wash Site Screener — Austin, gates-first

steps.say: I want help picking car wash sites to open
steps.reply:
I've recorded that question for you — quick recap while you decide: yesterday's screener got through **M0** (single Austin address → zoning/traffic/competitor gates with sources) and **M1** (all 7,710 eligible Travis County commercial/unincorporated parcels run through the same gates, near-misses explained), both verified passing. Someone removed the module today, before **M2** (revenue ranges for the sites that pass all gates) was built.

Let me know which way you want to go:
1. **Resume** — rebuild M0/M1 as they were and continue on to M2
2. **Start fresh** — a new plan, possibly different s

steps.say: It's for me, to decide which sites to pursue and brief my investors. Sites come from brokers by email. Today I check households within 3 miles, density, drive-time population, the traffic on the road and at the main intersection, then I score fourteen things like visibility and access from 1 to 10 with a note each, and write a memo to investors. Thresholds: 45,000 households, 30,000 cars a day. Start with Austin. Go ahead and write it up.
steps.reply:
I've drafted the workflow page — "Your workflow" card is now up for your review.

**Gist:** broker email → geocode → check households (3mi, 45,000 threshold) and road traffic (AADT, 30,000 threshold) → score 14 criteria 1–10 with notes → draft the investor memo for you to send. Candidate sites, their gate numbers, their scores and memo drafts are kept as separate linked tables.

Three things I couldn't know and put my pick on the card for: the exact 14 criteria (you'd named only visibility and access, so I proposed a trade-standard list), the drive-time band for drive-time population, and how

steps.say: Add a minimum lot size of 0.8 acres as one of the checks.
steps.reply: Added. The workflow page now checks lot size ≥ 0.8 acres — read from county parcel/assessor data (e.g. Travis County Appraisal District for Austin-area sites) — alongside the households and traffic checks; where a county doesn't publish acreage, it's flagged unverified rather than failed. The updated page is ready for your review.
